Department Information

California’s Department of Resources Recycling and Recovery (CalRecycle) brings together the state’s recycling and waste management programs to move the state towards a circular economy that reduces waste and reuses all materials.

Through landmark initiatives like the Integrated Waste Management Act and Beverage Container Recycling and Litter Reduction Act, California works toward a society that uses less, recycles more, and takes resource conservation to higher and higher levels.

CalRecycle’s Mission: Protecting California’s environment and climate for the health and prosperity of future generations through the reduction, reuse and recycling of California resources, environmental education, disaster recovery and the transition from a disposable to a fully circular economy.

CalRecycle values diversity, equity, and inclusion throughout the organization. We foster an environment where employees from a variety of backgrounds, cultures, and personal experiences are welcomed and can thrive. We believe the diversity of our employees is essential to inspiring innovative solutions. Together we further our mission to protect the environment and preserve resources by empowering Californians to reduce, reuse, and recycle. Join CalRecycle to improve the lives of all Californians.

Department Website: http://www.calrecycle.ca.gov

Job Description And Duties

CalRecycle’s Office of Environmental Justice, Tribal Relations, Education and Outreach is seeking a Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) to serve as a lead technical expert on environmental justice and tribal-relations issues. The incumbent will conduct advanced scientific analyses, guide departmentwide integration of environmental justice and tribal priorities, and lead complex evaluations of program impacts on California Native American tribes, disadvantaged communities, low-income populations, rural communities, and farmworkers. This role independently designs studies, performs advanced fieldwork, develops best-practice guidance, and advises leadership on emerging environmental challenges and policy opportunities.

The Senior Environmental Scientist will coordinate cross-division efforts to ensure consistency in environmental justice implementation, provide specialized training to staff, prepare high-level technical reports and public-facing materials, and lead outreach and partnership-building efforts with tribes, community organizations, and statewide partners. In addition, the incumbent may lead and support aspects of grant and contract management, including development of equity-focused criteria, technical review of proposals, and monitoring of project performance to ensure alignment with environmental justice and tribal priorities.

Occasional statewide travel is required, and the position participates in the DMV Employer Pull Notice Program.This position offers the opportunity to shape statewide environmental programs, strengthen equitable access to grants, support community-centered engagement strategies, and advance youth environmental education initiatives.

As of July 1st, 2026, the position is office-centered, and employees will be expected to report to the office at least four days per week.
T his position may be eligible for hybrid telework under Government Code 14200, subject to the candidate meeting telework eligibility criteria set forth in the CalEPA telework policy and/or future program needs. Employees not residing in California are not eligible for telework. jobs.title: Strategic Solutions Engineer - CNC - San Francisco, CA
jobs.description:
About MISUMI Americas

MISUMI Americas, a division of MISUMI Group, is a leading provider of standard, configurable, and custom manufacturing solutions. By integrating a vast catalog of components with a world-class digital manufacturing platform, MISUMI Americas empowers engineers and procurement teams to accelerate innovation across the entire product lifecycle. With operations in the San Francisco Bay Area and Chicago, the company serves as a vital partner for the most innovative companies in the Americas.

Impact In This Role

Misumi Americas is seeking a Strategic Solutions Engineer - CNC to join our solution engineering team focused on strategic, high-complexity, production-level customer programs. This role sits at the intersection of engineering, manufacturing, customer advisory, and commercial execution, supporting customers as they scale from prototype into production.

The ideal candidate brings deep experience in CNC machining, casting, CAD, (SolidWorks), GD&T, and DFM skills, strong technical communication skills, and the ability to guide customers through DFM/DFA, production readiness, operational/program support, cost optimization, and mechanical assembly considerations. This role is mainly customer-facing and requires comfort operating in ambiguous, high-stakes environments.

What You’ll Be Doing

Customer & Program/Production Support

Serve as a trusted technical advisor/guide for strategic customers with complex CNC manufacturing needs.
Lead technical scoping discussions, translating customer requirements into manufacturable, scalable solutions.
Some level of support for customers through prototype → production transitions, anticipating manufacturing risks early.

Manufacturing & DFM Expertise

Perform detailed DFM/DFA reviews for CNC-machined components.
Evaluate part geometry, tolerances, GD&T, material selection, and finish requirements for manufacturability and cost.
Provide cost optimization recommendations based on process selection, feature simplification, and volume scaling.
Support efforts with manufacturing-informed input on feasibility, risk, and lead time.

Assembly & System-Level Understanding/Support

Evaluate and guide on mechanical assemblies, including:
Part-to-part fit, stack-ups, and tolerance interactions
Fastener selection, joint design, and access for assembly
Assembly sequencing and installation considerations

Help customers identify risks related to assembly, serviceability, and field installation.
Provide feedback that improves downstream assembly efficiency and reduces rework.

Technical Execution

Review and interpret engineering drawings with strong command of GD&T.
Perform CAD work, including:
Design updates for manufacturability
Parametric 3D Modeling & Visualization
Detailed Documentation & Drafting with GD&T
Optimizing CAD — CNC to Casting and 3DP to IM
Reverse engineering

Collaborate cross-functionally with Sales, Operations, Quality, and LoB teams.

Quality & Compliance Awareness

Apply working knowledge of ISO 9001 and AS9100D requirements in customer discussions and internal workflows.
Identify quality risks early and ensure proper requirements definition (“quality in, quality out”).

Desired Traits

6+ years of relevant experience in manufacturing roles such as CNC (candidates with deeper experience are strongly encouraged to apply).
Bachelor's degree in Manufacturing Engineering or related field, or equivalent demonstrated hands-on experience.
Strong expertise in CNC machining processes (milling, turning, multi-axis) and Casting, .
Must have DFM, cost optimization, and manufacturing trade-off fluency.
Hands-on experience in production-scale manufacturing programs.
Proven ability to interpret and apply engineering drawings and GD&T.
Solid understanding of mechanical assemblies and installation considerations.
Experience supporting customer-facing technical discussions.
Familiarity with ISO 9001 and AS9100D compliance environments.
Willingness and ability to travel 30–40%.
Proficiency with Google Workspace and/or Microsoft Office.
Strong verbal, written, and digital communication skills.
SolidWorks CAD proficiency.
Willingness to perform hands-on CAD work and reverse engineering as needed.
Willingness to support the Marketing team with technical publications, seminars, university lectures, and other related activities as needed.

Nice-to-Have Qualifications

Experience with Casting, Molding (IM) and/or Additive Manufacturing (3DP).
Prior experience working with external suppliers or contract manufacturers.
Leverage AI tools (e.g., Claude and other AI assistants) to accelerate DFM analysis, documentation, customer-facing content creation, and day-to-day engineering workflows.
Experience integrating AI/LLM tools into engineering or customer-facing workflows.

Physical Demands

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Standard Office & Remote Work: Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer for remote customer consultations.
Onsite Environments: Must be able to walk and stand on manufacturing floors and trade show environments for extended periods. Must be able to safely navigate industrial areas around heavy machinery and wear required PPE (safety glasses, safety shoes, hearing protection).
Lifting & Handling: Ability to occasionally lift, move, and position mechanical parts, prototypes, or trade show materials weighing up to 30 lbs.

Perks and Benefits

Competitive medical, dental, and vision insurance
401K plan
Parental leave programs
Paid volunteer days
And much, much more!

Salary Range: $125,000 to $142,000 per year, based upon experience

Interested in learning more? We look forward to hearing from you soon.

Bring diverse perspectives and experience to our culture and company.
Excel at being part of a strong, empathetic team.
Thrive in an environment emphasizing respect, honesty, collaboration, and growth.
Have an ‘always learning’ mindset that celebrates learning, not just wins.
Help us continue to build a world-class organization that values the contributions of all of our teammates

We encourage applications from members of underrepresented groups, including but not limited to women, members of the LGBTQ community, people of color, people with disabilities, and veterans.

jobs.title: Field Readiness Lead, Solutions Engineering
jobs.description:
Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors to first responders, soldiers in battlefield scenarios, and beyond.

About The Role

Skydio is seeking an experienced operations leader to join our team as Manager, Solutions Operations. This role owns the technical operations the Solutions Engineering organization runs on: the headquarters demo program and the aircraft, docks, and environment behind it, the capture of flight, imagery, and integration content, and the library that holds all of it. You will lead live demonstrations for VIP customers, partners, and government visitors alongside Skydio leadership on a regular basis, and you will use what you own to bring new Solutions Engineers and Solutions Specialists up to speed and keep the field current on new capability.

This role is cross vertical. It touches every part of Solutions Engineering across National Security, SLED, Commercial, and the Launch Team, and it works with the account teams, Engineering, Product, Customer Success, Training, and Sales Enablement those teams depend on. The hard part is pace and breadth. Product ships faster than any one SE can track, the organization is hiring across the globe, and each vertical has its own customers and workflows. This seat is how the demo standard, the content, and the ramp stay consistent without four directors rebuilding the same thing.

This role is based at Skydio headquarters in San Mateo, California.
Travel of approximately 15% is required to capture content in the field, support field teams, and support company events. If you have most of what is listed below and are confident you can learn the rest, we want to hear from you.

This role reports to the VP, Solutions Engineering.

About The Team

Solutions Engineering is the technical arm of Skydio's go-to-market motion. We sit between the customer and the product: turning operational problems into program designs, proving capability in the field, and making sure Skydio's products are used, integrated, and flown at scale.

This seat is measured on the readiness and quality of the demonstrations that run out of headquarters, on how current and used the content library is, and on time to productivity for new Solutions Engineers and Specialists.

Solutions Engineers are critical members of the Skydio organization and work closely with Key Account Leaders, Engineering, and Product to support deal progression, customer confidence, successful deployments, and the long-term success of Public Safety sUAS programs.

How You'll Make An Impact

Run the HQ demo program

Lead live demonstrations at headquarters for VIP customers, customer summits, partners, press, and government visitors, presenting with Skydio executives, from a short flight to a full dock and command software walkthroughs.
Own the demo environment: aircraft, docks, network, controllers, and props, plus the pre-flight discipline that keeps a demonstration from failing in front of a chief.
Maintain airworthiness, batteries, firmware, and spares so the fleet is ready to fly on short notice, and coordinate demo scheduling and dock availability with the teams that share the site.
Set the demo standard the rest of the organization runs against.

Own the content and the library

Plan and run capture missions, including flights, imagery, scans, and dock deployments, that produce the footage, data, and screenshots the whole organization uses.
Build demo scripts, reference architectures, and trial plan templates out of what the strongest Solutions Engineers already do, rather than inventing a parallel standard.
Own the library. One place, one version, findable in under a minute. Run a review cadence against the release calendar, retire what is stale, and track what actually gets used.
Capture integration and competitive material: what the platforms our customers already run actually do, where Skydio wins, and what an honest answer sounds like where it does not.

Enable the team

Own onboarding for new Solutions Engineers and Solutions Specialists: the curriculum, hands-on flight and dock time, the shadowing plan, and the checkpoints that tell a manager a new hire is ready to run a customer engagement alone.
Ingest new product and technical developments as they land, get hands on with pre-release capability, and translate each release into what the field needs to know, say, and show.
Work across every vertical and function. Build enablement once, in a form each team can adapt, and partner with Sales Enablement and Training so the field gets one coordinated program.

Represent the customer inside Skydio

Be a source of ground truth on how the product actually demonstrates and how quickly people can learn it. You will see every rough edge repeatedly, and earlier than almost anyone.
Turn what you see into prioritized, defensible feedback to Product and Engineering rather than a list of one-off asks.

What Makes You a Good Fit

5+ years in a technical operations, field operations, customer-facing technical, or enablement role.
Hands-on sUAS operating experience and the judgment to fly safely and legally in front of an audience.
Comfortable presenting live to senior executives and customers, and steady when something does not go to plan.
A track record of building technical content or programs that other people actually used.
Fast at learning new technology and clear at explaining it, and comfortable working across many teams with different customers, priorities, and vocabulary.
Familiarity with DFR concepts of operation and dock based remote operations.
Organized and consistent. A demo fleet, a library, and a ramp program only work when someone maintains them.
Lead by example. Willing to do whatever is needed to get a customer situation resolved.

Nice to Have

Experience running a demo center, lab, or fleet operation.
Prior public safety service or agency UAS program experience.
Experience with dock-based, remote, or BVLOS operations at scale.
Video and photo production skills for demo and enablement content.
Working knowledge of public safety technologies such as CAD and VMS, or of Salesforce and learning platforms such as Uplimit.

What Is Required

FAA Part 107 Certificate, or the ability to obtain one within 60 days of hire.
Ability to work on site at Skydio headquarters in San Mateo, California.
Ability to travel approximately 15% of the time.
Ability to lift up to 60 lbs unaided.

Compensation:

Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors to first responders, soldiers in battlefield scenarios, and beyond.

About The Role

Skydio is seeking an experienced operations leader to join our team as Manager, Solutions Operations. This role owns the technical operations the Solutions Engineering organization runs on: the headquarters demo program and the aircraft, docks, and environment behind it, the capture of flight, imagery, and integration content, and the library that holds all of it. You will lead live demonstrations for VIP customers, partners, and government visitors alongside Skydio leadership on a regular basis, and you will use what you own to bring new Solutions Engineers and Solutions Specialists up to speed and keep the field current on new capability.

This role is cross vertical. It touches every part of Solutions Engineering across National Security, SLED, Commercial, and the Launch Team, and it works with the account teams, Engineering, Product, Customer Success, Training, and Sales Enablement those teams depend on. The hard part is pace and breadth. Product ships faster than any one SE can track, the organization is hiring across the globe, and each vertical has its own customers and workflows. This seat is how the demo standard, the content, and the ramp stay consistent without four directors rebuilding the same thing.

This role is based at Skydio headquarters in San Mateo, California.
Travel of approximately 15% is required to capture content in the field, support field teams, and support company events. If you have most of what is listed below and are confident you can learn the rest, we want to hear from you.

This role reports to the VP, Solutions Engineering.

About The Team

Solutions Engineering is the technical arm of Skydio's go-to-market motion. We sit between the customer and the product: turning operational problems into program designs, proving capability in the field, and making sure Skydio's products are used, integrated, and flown at scale.

This seat is measured on the readiness and quality of the demonstrations that run out of headquarters, on how current and used the content library is, and on time to productivity for new Solutions Engineers and Specialists.

Solutions Engineers are critical members of the Skydio organization and work closely with Key Account Leaders, Engineering, and Product to support deal progression, customer confidence, successful deployments, and the long-term success of Public Safety sUAS programs.

How You'll Make An Impact

Run the HQ demo program

Lead live demonstrations at headquarters for VIP customers, customer summits, partners, press, and government visitors, presenting with Skydio executives, from a short flight to a full dock and command software walkthroughs.
Own the demo environment: aircraft, docks, network, controllers, and props, plus the pre-flight discipline that keeps a demonstration from failing in front of a chief.
Maintain airworthiness, batteries, firmware, and spares so the fleet is ready to fly on short notice, and coordinate demo scheduling and dock availability with the teams that share the site.
Set the demo standard the rest of the organization runs against.

Own the content and the library

Plan and run capture missions, including flights, imagery, scans, and dock deployments, that produce the footage, data, and screenshots the whole organization uses.
Build demo scripts, reference architectures, and trial plan templates out of what the strongest Solutions Engineers already do, rather than inventing a parallel standard.
Own the library. One place, one version, findable in under a minute. Run a review cadence against the release calendar, retire what is stale, and track what actually gets used.
Capture integration and competitive material: what the platforms our customers already run actually do, where Skydio wins, and what an honest answer sounds like where it does not.

Enable the team

Own onboarding for new Solutions Engineers and Solutions Specialists: the curriculum, hands-on flight and dock time, the shadowing plan, and the checkpoints that tell a manager a new hire is ready to run a customer engagement alone.
Ingest new product and technical developments as they land, get hands on with pre-release capability, and translate each release into what the field needs to know, say, and show.
Work across every vertical and function. Build enablement once, in a form each team can adapt, and partner with Sales Enablement and Training so the field gets one coordinated program.

Represent the customer inside Skydio

Be a source of ground truth on how the product actually demonstrates and how quickly people can learn it. You will see every rough edge repeatedly, and earlier than almost anyone.
Turn what you see into prioritized, defensible feedback to Product and Engineering rather than a list of one-off asks.

What Makes You a Good Fit

5+ years in a technical operations, field operations, customer-facing technical, or enablement role.
Hands-on sUAS operating experience and the judgment to fly safely and legally in front of an audience.
Comfortable presenting live to senior executives and customers, and steady when something does not go to plan.
A track record of building technical content or programs that other people actually used.
Fast at learning new technology and clear at explaining it, and comfortable working across many teams with different customers, priorities, and vocabulary.
Familiarity with DFR concepts of operation and dock based remote operations.
Organized and consistent. A demo fleet, a library, and a ramp program only work when someone maintains them.
Lead by example. Willing to do whatever is needed to get a customer situation resolved.

Nice to Have

Experience running a demo center, lab, or fleet operation.
Prior public safety service or agency UAS program experience.
Experience with dock-based, remote, or BVLOS operations at scale.
Video and photo production skills for demo and enablement content.
Working knowledge of public safety technologies such as CAD and VMS, or of Salesforce and learning platforms such as Uplimit.

What Is Required

FAA Part 107 Certificate, or the ability to obtain one within 60 days of hire.
Ability to work on site at Skydio headquarters in San Mateo, California.
Ability to travel approximately 15% of the time.
Ability to lift up to 60 lbs unaided.

Compensation will vary based on factors, including skill level, proficiencies, transferable knowledge, and experience. The annual base salary range for this position is $170,000 - $215,000*. POSITION OBJECTIVE

The Database Manager will provide oversight, strategic planning, coordination, and maintenance for the Patient Care and Research Database working group of the Center for AIDS Research at Case Western University/University Hospitals of Cleveland Case Medical Center.

Essential Functions

Ensure the timely review, update, and critical analysis of all clinical data derived from the provider-patient interactions involving the patients of the Special Immunology Unit and the research participants in studies conducted at the University Hospitals of Cleveland Case Medical Center Clinical Trials Unit. (10%)
Establish and conduct a regular mechanism for critical extraction of relevant data from the electronic and printed medical records for all patients followed at the Special Immunology Unit and all research participants whose records are to be maintained through the patient care and research database. This function requires the ability to understand the basics of medical care for patients with HIV infection and related conditions, and to identify critically ambiguous or inconsistent data elements in the medical record for further review. (10%)
Administer the flow of information to and from researchers who request data from the Patient Care and Research Database and respond to the needs of the investigators and research staff of the Clinical Trials Unit to identify and follow potential participants for clinical studies. (7%)
Supervise the compliance with, and design and enforce the unit¿s policies about patient confidentiality, data integrity, and data safety. (7%)
Together with the IT staff and programming personnel, design, update, and maintain the queries and programs needed to respond to both the clinical and research objectives of the unit¿s investigators and providers. (7%)
Supervise the performance, effectiveness, and progress of the patient care and research staff, including but not limited to the assistant database manager and any undergraduate programming students asked to be part of the PCRD team on a temporary basis. (7%)
Identify areas for targeted improvement of processes and tools in the Patient Care and Research Database system in response to both the day-to-day workflow and the comments and input from users and program managers. (7%)
Establish and lead periodic reviews of data quality in the Patient Care and Research Database, including all members of the database team and additional ad-hoc participants as needed. (7%)
Propose and lead the implementation of solutions to new needs and desired functionality in the Patient Care and Research Database. (6%)

Nonessential Functions

Communicate directly with healthcare providers, clinic administrators, and ancillary personnel, to resolve data inconsistencies or unclear information related to patient and research participant records. (5%)
Maintain an accurate and systematic tracking mechanism of all the research activities related to the Patient Care and Research Database. (5%)
Maintain and lead the monthly database meeting with users, program directors, and clinic providers, and manage the implementation of responses to items raised during the meetings. (5%)
Interact with local, regional, national, and international investigators and collaborators in designing solutions for clinical and research data management that contribute to the mission of the Case Western Reserve University/University Hospitals of Cleveland Case Medical Center HIV research group. (5%)
Collaborate with providers, clinical leaders, and administrators in the Special Immunology Unit to fulfill funding agency requirements and emerging clinical needs to optimize care and services for clinic patients. (5%)
Initiate, and respond to requests for, communication with the unit administrative personnel related to budgetary issues, unit personnel coordination, equipment, and office supplies. (4%)
Cross-cover the functions of other Patient Care and Research Database team members during absences. (2%)
Perform other duties as assigned. (1%)

CONTACTS

Department: Department: Daily contact with other Patient Care and Research Database team members. Regular contact with physicians, other healthcare providers, and ancillary personnel in the Special Immunology unit. Regular contact with investigators, research nurses, and laboratory personnel affiliated with the Center for AIDS Research and the Clinical Trials Unit.

University: Some contact with Case Western Reserve University administrative offices of Human Resources, Payroll, or Student Employment as needed to manage the team and the position.

External: Occasional contact with external collaborators, including foreign collaborators and care providers, as needed to fulfill the requirements of multicenter projects.

Students: Intermittent contact with students hired to perform programming and/or clerical functions in the PCRD team.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITY

This position directly supervises the assistant Database Manager and any-programming assistant and/or clerical positions in the Patient Care and Research Database team.

Qualifications

Experience: 4 years of experience in related fields. Experience can be any combination of work as a healthcare provider with direct contact and day-today management of medical records, clinical research data management, electronic medical record management, and clinical database management.

Education: Bachelor¿s degree required. Master¿s degree or higher is strongly preferred. Degrees in a healthcare discipline, computing with an emphasis in database management, or healthcare administration with an emphasis in electronic medical records are also strongly preferred.

Required Skills

Proven understanding of medical terminology and familiarity with medical records and medical documents.
Knowledge of HIV-related medications, conditions, and terminology highly desirable.
Proven ability to analyze data and identify patterns.
Professional and effective verbal and written communication skills. Ability to interact with colleagues, supervisors, and customers face to face.
Strong interpersonal skills; ability to work and communicate with various individuals from a broad spectrum of disciplines, technical and educational backgrounds within the department, school and university, and with individuals outside the university.
Strong organization skills; ability to multi-task, prioritize, give attention to detail, and meet deadlines.
Effective management skills; ability to lead, work with, elicit cooperation from, and read communication styles of team members and staff. Ability to lead a small but dynamic working group effectively and efficiently is essential.
Ability to work effectively independently and collaboratively within a team.
Ability to problem-solve effectively, and demonstrate good judgment and logical decision-making. Must demonstrate high creativity and ability to envision solutions to novel problems and requirements with minimal supervision, and to evaluate and adjust proposed strategies rapidly and efficiently.
Ability to conform to shifting priorities, demands and timeline. Must be flexible in order to respond to project adjustments and alterations promptly and efficiently. Must be able to adapt to varying workloads and respond appropriately to stressful situations.
Ability to quickly learn new techniques, processes, procedures, techniques, ideas, etc., including medical guidelines, related to job functions and assigned projects.
Advanced knowledge of the Windows operating system and basic MS Office software in a network environment.
Proficiency in the use of database management systems, including Microsoft SQL and Microsoft Access, are strongly desirable and will be given priority. For applicants without these skills, willingness to receive training in these applications early during appointment.
Ability to demonstrate successful support, education, and advocacy for all students, aligned with the values, mission, and messaging of the university, while adhering to the staff policy on conflict of commitment and interest.
Ability to meet consistent attendance.
Ability to interact with colleagues, supervisors, and customers face to face.
Willingness to learn and work with Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools and technologies.

WORKING CONDITIONS

General office environment with frequent computer use. Occasional travel, including internationally, may be required as needed.

This position is eligible for hybrid work arrangement up to two remote days per week at the discretion of the department. New employees may begin a hybrid schedule upon approval from the supervisor, successful completion of an orientation period and signing the remote work checklist certification form.
